thread:
kevin (Acme): hitting a bunch of 429s since this morning. only started after we moved some traffic behind our new NAT pool.
kevin (Acme): sample error: \"rate_limit_exceeded\" on identical requests, but our dashboard shows quota left on the API key.
kevin (Acme): we alternate between sending the API key in Authorization header and an older project-scoped token in query param while we roll forward. could that cause mixing?
jamie (support): sorry for the trouble — sending this to infra to look. can you paste a curl that reproduces the failing request and the exact 429 headers?
kevin (Acme): yup:```\ncurl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'\n```\nkevin (Acme): response headers we see: `x-rate-limit-scope: ip`, `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`, `x-request-id: r-7f3c`
jamie (support): interesting — header says requests were accounted to IP. that usually means the key wasn't accepted or was missing when we evaluated quota. can you try the same curl with `-v` to confirm the outgoing Authorization header reaches our edge?
kevin (Acme): running `curl -v` shows `Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-abc123` in the client send. but on our side there's a corporate proxy that rewrites some headers.
opsbot: alert: spike in 429s for customer acme (r-7f3c, r-7f3d, r-7f42) — NAT egress 35.4.152.0/28 showing bursts.
marco (eng-infra): @jamie fyi: auth precedence is Key > Project token > IP fallback. if the header is stripped before reaching our auth stage, the request falls back to IP-based quota and NAT pools can exhaust quickly.
marco (eng-infra): can you share full request-id logs? we can check how our edge classified them. jamie, can you pull r-7f3c?
jamie (support): pulled trace for r-7f3c — shows incoming connection from 35.4.152.19, no `authorization` header at edge, classified as anonymous -> ip scope.
jamie (support): kevin, looks like your gateway is dropping the Authorization header during TLS termination / proxying or you're using a header whitelist.
kevin (Acme): ah, we do have an egress policy that strips `Authorization` on certain routes for inspection. not ideal.
lisa (billing): quick Q: if we move to per-key quota bump while this is fixed, will billing change? we need to advise Acme on cost/limits.
jamie (support): short answer: per-key quota increases are possible but we need an internal review. meanwhile the fastest workaround is to ensure Authorization reaches us (disable strip) or to add a project-level override (we can temporarily pin requests from their NAT to a higher burst allowance).
marco (eng-infra): repro steps for customer to confirm behavior: 1) curl with Authorization header directly to our edge IP (skip proxy) -> should show `x-rate-limit-scope: key`. 2) curl through proxy -> shows `x-rate-limit-scope: ip`. 3) run `tcpdump -A` on proxy to confirm header strip. share pcap if needed.
kevin (Acme): doing step 1 now — direct curl shows `x-rate-limit-scope: key` and no 429s. step 2 reproduces 429 quickly.
jamie (support): ok confirmed. next actions: (a) @kevin ask infra to stop stripping Authorization for this route; (b) @jamie will open a temporary NAT-whitelist request (ops team) to raise burst limits for 35.4.152.0/28 for 48h; (c) @marco will file an internal note recommending customers send `x-client-id` header we can map for NAT scenarios.
marco (eng-infra): note: long term we want customers to use keys and keep them intact; we also support mapping a static header for NAT pools but it's less secure. we've had one other customer do a proxy-friendly token header.
kevin (Acme): thanks — we'll patch our proxy rules. also can you confirm logs we should share if we still see 429s after the change?
jamie (support): if it persists, share `x-request-id` values and a full `curl -v` transcript and a `tcpdump` snippet showing missing header. we'll escalate to infra with those.
kevin (Acme): patched the proxy to forward Authorization. retesting now, sending r-7f90 as new request id.
opsbot: resolved alert: 429 spike for acme subsided.
kevin (Acme): confirmed: requests now show `x-rate-limit-scope: key` and no 429. thanks! :tada:
jamie (support): great — closing on our side. follow-ups: lisa will handle any short-term quota/billing adjustments if they request a temporary uplift. marco will draft internal doc for NAT + auth guidance.
lisa (billing): noted — @kevin if you want a temporary quota uptick while you roll this change out to all clusters, DM me your account id.
kevin (Acme): will do, thanks team.
